emma (sales): quick heads-up — Globex POC started seeing intermittent TLS hostname errors and 502s after we flipped the private endpoint routing. Can we swarm?

carlos (customer): Repro from our app: resolve `api.globex.internal` via private resolver -> connect to VPCE -> after we switched the split-horizon record a subset of requests fail with `x509: certificate is valid for redwood-internal, not api.globex.internal` and then occasional 502s. Happens ~3-7% of calls, unpredictable.

anita (eng-network): ok can you paste output of `dig +short api.globex.internal` from the app host and an `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.globex.internal -showcerts` from a failing request? Also include target group health.

carlos (customer): dig inside VPC returns CNAME `vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-abcdef.vpce.amazonaws.com` -> 10.240.12.8 (NLB). Public resolver returns 54.234.12.45 for some tests. Target group shows two targets healthy.

carlos (customer): openssl from a failing trace (sanitized):
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = redwood-internal
verify error:num=62:hostname mismatch
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-internal
   i:/CN=redwood-root-ca

anita (eng-network): hostname mismatch usually means the server presented a cert without the requested SAN. Two quick possibilities: 1) one of the target instances is serving a default cert (old canary), or 2) something in the path is rewriting SNI (sidecar/proxy). Any sidecars or mTLS proxies in your pod/instance?

carlos (customer): we do run an Envoy sidecar in the app that mTLSs outbound traffic and we recently rolled a canary of the backend. Didn't think SNI would change, but the sidecar injects the service account name into SNI for some telemetry reasons.

leo (solutions): that matches. If sidecar replaces SNI with an internal name and the backend presents a cert for that internal name, you'll see intermittent hostname mismatch depending on which backend instance is hit. Mitigations: a) ensure all backend certs include both SANs (api.globex.internal + internal name), b) configure sidecar to preserve original SNI for calls to PrivateLink hosts, or c) temporarily pin NLB to the stable target group.

anita (eng-network): also confirm TLS termination location: NLB is TCP/Pass-through so certs live on targets. If canary used default cert, that would explain 502s when the backend rejects the request.

carlos (customer): confirmed: canary backend has default cert CN `redwood-internal`. We missed cert rotation for that deployment.

emma (sales): customer asked if we can do a quick mitigation while they fix canary certs and also asked about Dedicated trial pricing for validating PrivateLink behavior.

leo (solutions): immediate options: we can pin the NLB to the stable target group for your POC window. For Dedicated trial: we offer a 7-14 day engineer-backed reserved pool (small capacity). Ballpark for a short trial is $120-160/day — will confirm exact number with finance and DM you. I can also provision a trial env once paper is signed.

carlos (customer): pinning to stable targets and updating the canary certs sounds good. Please send pricing and a short KMS/audit one-pager for our SOC.

anita (eng-network): ops follow-ups: 1) add checklist item to POC runbook to verify cert SANs on every canary/stable release, 2) add note about sidecars that rewrite SNI and how to opt-out, 3) add `openssl` troubleshooting snippet: `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts | sed -n '1,60p'`. I'll open a PR for the docs.

ops-bot: ticket POC-7001 created and assigned to eng-network for checklist + docs updates.

leo (solutions): I'll DM the security one-pager (KMS/HSM, TLS in transit, audit logs) and confirm pricing by EOD.

emma (sales): Next steps: carlos to rotate canary certs and confirm retest, leo to send security docs + pricing, anita to PR checklist updates. Marking this thread resolved for now — re-open if errors persist. :thumbsup:
